final_answer.key_evidence_summary: Symptom pointer: alerts on ts-contacts-service report HTTP 503 Service Unavailable (20x each on GET /api/v1/contactservice/contacts/account/{userId} and POST /api/v1/contactservice/contacts), and an active TCP probe against the Service-declared port 12347 fails from worker-01/02/03 ('Connection Failed'). The victim's own signal shows the break: 'ts-contacts-service ENDPOINTS <none>', and the pod inventory contains no ts-contacts-service pod although all other 41 business pods are 2/2 Running. The owner chain isolates the single outlier: deployment ts-contacts-service is 0/0 (0 up-to-date, 0 available) while every other workload is 1/1; DescribeResource gives 'Replicas: 0 desired | 0 updated | 0 total | 0 available' with 'NewReplicaSet: ts-contacts-service-7fc68f4bbc (0/0 replicas created)'. Mechanism event binds it literally: 'ScalingReplicaSet deployment/ts-contacts-service Scaled down replica set ts-contacts-service-7fc68f4bbc to 0 from 1' together with 'Killing pod/ts-contacts-service-7fc68f4bbc-bwjc4' and 'SuccessfulDelete replicaset/...'. This is the only scale-to-zero never followed by a scale-up (ts-travel-service was likewise scaled to 0 but recovered: 'Scaled up replica set ts-travel-service-5b9b99c879 to 1', its pod Running). Config closure: selector app=ts-contacts-service matches the pod template label, containerPort 12347 matches the Service port 12347, image/Secret(ts-contacts-mysql)/ConfigMap(nacos) references all present and resolvable - so the break is not scheduling, admission, image, probe or addressing, but the replica count itself being driven to 0, leaving the Service with no endpoints and callers with 503. Downstream 500s on ts-preserve-service and ts-inside-payment-service are consistent consequences of the contacts path being down.
